mechanism_narrative: The sharp decline in RETAIL_REC mobility in the most recent week, following a period of relative stability, indicates a negative momentum that will persist, leading to lower retail and recreation activity over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than the average of the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in residential mobility, indicating more people staying home, directly correlates with reduced out-of-home activities. If RESIDENTIAL remains elevated, RETAIL_REC will continue to decline over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL increases by more than 1.5 points week-on-week and stays above 10%
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL drops below 9% in the next two weeks, and RETAIL_REC subsequently rises.

mechanism_narrative: The combined recent decline in both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT mobility suggests a reduction in daily commuting and general movement, which will suppress incidental retail and recreation visits, leading to lower RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: Both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT mobility increase by more than 2 points each in the next two weeks, and RETAIL_REC rises.

mechanism_narrative: The sharp drop in PARKS mobility, combined with the general decline in other outdoor activities, suggests a shift towards more cautious behavior or unfavorable weather, which will keep RETAIL_REC low in the short term.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls below -20% and stays there
failure_condition: PARKS mobility recovers above -15% within the next two weeks, and RETAIL_REC shows an upward trend.

mechanism_narrative: The recent significant drop in GROCERY_PHARM mobility, often a proxy for essential errands, indicates a broader reduction in out-of-home trips that will negatively impact non-essential retail and recreation over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM mobility recovers above 20% in the next two weeks, and RETAIL_REC rises.

mechanism_narrative: While WORKPLACES mobility has shown a slight recovery in the last two weeks, it remains significantly below baseline. This insufficient return to workplaces will prevent a meaningful recovery in associated retail and recreation, keeping RETAIL_REC low over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES remains between -16% and -14% for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: WORKPLACES mobility rises above -10% within the next two weeks, leading to an increase in RETAIL_REC.

mechanism_narrative: The inverse relationship between RESIDENTIAL and RETAIL_REC mobility, where a rise in people staying home directly corresponds to a fall in out-of-home activities, will continue to drive RETAIL_REC down as RESIDENTIAL remains elevated.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL is above 10% and RETAIL_REC is below -20%
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL drops below 9% while RETAIL_REC simultaneously rises above -18% in the next week.

mechanism_narrative: The widespread decline across multiple out-of-home categories (RETAIL_REC, GROCERY_PHARM, PARKS, TRANSIT) in the latest week suggests a broad shift in public behavior, possibly due to new advisories or general caution, which will keep RETAIL_REC suppressed over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: At least three of the four out-of-home categories (RETAIL_REC, GROCERY_PHARM, PARKS, TRANSIT) show a positive week-on-week change in the next two weeks.
